title: fix(app-shell): show Studio nav entries in the menu's order, and let a canvas drag write order
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ882oEE1FPo1aN5yzd2Gp32G)_
Fixes #26979

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:Studio「界面」左栏导航树与导航编辑画布,改为按 `order` 排列,与运行时菜单一致;画布拖拽排序时必要时写入被拖条目的 `order`。
- 为什么改:运行时菜单按 `order` 排序,Studio 却按数组顺序显示,设置了 `order` 的条目在设计器和发布后的菜单里位置不同,拖拽也可能看不出效果。
- 风险与回滚:只动 app-shell(私有包)三处源码加测试;没有设置 `order` 的应用显示与拖拽结果不变;回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`AppNavCanvas.tsx` 的 `moveItem` 与 `inMenuOrder`;`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` 的 `NavTree`;新测试块 `railNavOrder-26979`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.railLabels.test.tsx -t railNavOrder`,预期 4 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- The Studio Interfaces rail (`NavTree`) and the nav canvas (`AppNavCanvas`) list every level through one new helper, `inMenuOrder` (exported from `AppNavCanvas.tsx`): `order` ascending, an absent `order` as `0`, ties in authored order. That is the running menu's rule, `byNavOrder` in `@object-ui/layout`, which the sidebar applies at the top level and inside each group. Selection ids, renames and removals still address the authored array index.
- A canvas drop rewrites the root array in the new shown order and writes the moved entry's `order` only when its current weight no longer falls between its new neighbours'; it then takes its neighbour's weight and the stable sort keeps it where it was dropped. At most one `order` write per drop, and none for an app whose entries carry no `order`.
- `NavNode` (`navSurface.ts`) and the canvas's `RawNav` declare the spec's `order?: number`, type only.

### Why this shape (the card's two options, measured)

- The menu sorts by `order` at every level, stably. A drag that only rewrote `order` (shape b) cannot fix entries whose `order` was written by the API or the inspector before any drag: the rail and canvas would still list array order. So both lists sort (shape a), and then a drag has to write `order` or it does nothing visible. Normalising the array to the shown order lets one neighbour-weight write place the entry, which is the fewest `order` writes that keeps the builder equal to the menu.
- `byNavOrder` is not imported: `navOrder.ts` is internal to `@object-ui/layout` and publishing it would widen that package's entry point. Per the seat's claim amendment on the card, Studio states the same rule locally and a test renders `NavigationRenderer` beside the rail and the canvas over the same entries, so the two rules cannot drift without a red test.
- `AppNavCanvas` is shared with Setup's app editor (`AppPreview.tsx`), which mounts the same component: the sorted listing and the drop behaviour are the same there.

## Tests

`StudioDesignSurface.railNavOrder-26979` in `StudioDesignSurface.railLabels.test.tsx` renders the real `InterfacesPillar` rail, `AppNavCanvas` and `NavigationRenderer`:

- entries with `order` [3, 1, 2] plus a group whose children carry [2, 1] read in one order on all three;
- a drag in the canvas leaves all three agreeing, and only the moved entry changes (it gains `order`; every other entry is the same object);
- control: entries without `order` keep array order, and a drag among them writes no `order`.

Ablations (each self-restoring through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, blob equal to HEAD after restore):

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| `inMenuOrder` stops sorting | 2 of 4 red (agreement, drag) |
| the drop's `order` write removed | 1 of 4 red (drag) |
| `NavTree` lists array order | 2 of 4 red (agreement, drag) |

The first attempt at the sort ablation was refused by the tool (its replacement text already occurred in the file), so it did not run; it was rerun with a distinct replacement.

## Acceptance notes

- Not changed, outside the file surface: on load the Interfaces pillar opens the first resolvable leaf of the authored array (`firstLeaf` in the load effect), which can now differ from the rail's first row when `order` reorders the top. Observation only.
- No changeset: the diff touches only `@object-ui/app-shell`, which is `private: true`.
